page:
Manual HMR (Hot Module Replacement) API for client-side module updates. Exposed via import.meta.hot object. For server-side HMR handling, see handleHotUpdate plugin hook.
- Conditional guard: if (import.meta.hot) required for tree-shaking in production
- import.meta.hot: ViteHotContext interface
- ViteHotContext methods: accept(), dispose(), prune(), invalidate(), on(), off(), send()
- ModuleNamespace type from 'vite/types/hot.d.ts'
- CustomEventName, InferCustomEventPayload from 'vite/types/customEvent.d.ts'
- accept(): self-accept without callback
- accept(cb): self-accept with callback receiving updated module
- accept(dep, cb): accept specific dependency, dep is module path string
- accept(deps, cb): accept array of dependencies
- dispose(cb): cleanup persistent side effects
- prune(cb): cleanup when module no longer imported
- invalidate(message?): force propagate update to importers
- on(event, cb): listen to HMR events
- off(event, cb): remove event listener
- send(event, data?): send custom event to server
- HMR events: 'vite:beforeUpdate', 'vite:afterUpdate', 'vite:beforeFullReload', 'vite:beforePrune', 'vite:invalidate', 'vite:error', 'vite:ws:disconnect', 'vite:ws:connect'
- data object: persisted across HMR instances, mutations visible to next instance
- TypeScript: add 'vite/client' to tsconfig.json types
- Backward compatibility: decline() is noop
- User responsibility: implement HMR acceptance in frameworks not handling it
How do I implement HMR in my modules? What HMR events are available? How do I send custom events to the server? How do I dispose side effects during HMR?

sections.manifest:
Required conditional guard for HMR.
- if (import.meta.hot) guard: required for all HMR API usage
- Allows tree-shaking in production
- Code inside guard removed in production builds
Why is the conditional guard required?

TypeScript IntelliSense for HMR.
- import.meta.hot type definitions in vite/client.d.ts
- Add 'vite/client' to tsconfig.json compilerOptions.types
- Enables TypeScript autocomplete and validation
How do I get TypeScript support for HMR?

Module self-acceptance with accept().
- import.meta.hot.accept(callback): self-accept hot updates
- Callback receives updated module (newModule)
- HMR boundary: module marked as accepting updates
- Module graph visualization: imports form edges
- Vite doesn't swap original module: responsibility to handle re-exports
- Simplified HMR: skip expensive proxy module generation
- Importers up chain not notified of changes
- Static analysis requirement: appear as import.meta.hot.accept( (whitespace-sensitive)
How do I make a module self-accepting?

Accepting updates from dependencies.
- import.meta.hot.accept(dep, cb): accept specific dependency updates
- dep: module path string (e.g., './foo.js')
- Callback receives updated dependency module
- Can accept array of deps: ['./foo.js', './bar.js']
- Callback receives array of updated modules (non-null only for updated)
- Array empty if update unsuccessful (syntax error)
How do I accept updates from specific dependencies?

Disposing side effects during HMR.
- import.meta.hot.dispose(cb): cleanup persistent side effects
- Called when updated copy is about to be replaced
- Useful for cleaning up timers, subscriptions, etc.
How do I clean up side effects during HMR?

Pruning modules from page.
- import.meta.hot.prune(cb): cleanup when module no longer imported
- Compared to dispose(): for code that self-cleans on updates
- Only needed cleanup when removed from page
- Vite uses for .css imports
When do I use prune instead of dispose?

Persistent data across HMR.
- import.meta.hot.data: object persisted across HMR instances
- Mutations visible to next module instance
- One data object per module path
- Re-assignment not supported (data = {...} doesn't work)
- Mutate properties instead: hot.data.someValue = 'hello'
- Cleared after hot.dispose/hot.prune callbacks complete
- New empty object on re-import
How do I persist data across HMR?

Declining HMR (backward compatibility).
- import.meta.hot.decline(): currently noop, backward compatibility
- Indicate module not hot-updatable: use hot.invalidate() instead
What does decline() do?

Invalidating self-accepting modules.
- import.meta.hot.invalidate(message?): force update propagation to importers
- Self-accepting module can't handle update at runtime
- HMR server invalidates importers (as if not self-accepting)
- Logs message in browser console and terminal
- Pass message for context on why invalidation happened
- Always call accept() first (or inside callback) for HMR listening
- Recommend calling invalidate() within accept() callback
How do I invalidate a module?

Listening to HMR events.
- import.meta.hot.on(event, cb): listen to HMR events
- Automatic Vite events: 'vite:beforeUpdate', 'vite:afterUpdate', 'vite:beforeFullReload', 'vite:beforePrune', 'vite:invalidate', 'vite:error', 'vite:ws:disconnect', 'vite:ws:connect'
- Custom events from plugins via handleHotUpdate
- Payload type inferred from CustomEventMap
What HMR events can I listen to?

Removing HMR event listeners.
- import.meta.hot.off(event, cb): remove callback from event listeners
- Same callback reference must be used
How do I remove event listeners?

Sending custom events to server.
- import.meta.hot.send(event, data?): send custom event to server
- Buffers data if not yet connected
- Sent once connection established
- See Client-server Communication in api-plugin.html for details
- Typing custom events: extend CustomEventMap interface
How do I send custom events to the server?

Further HMR learning resources.
- 'Hot Module Replacement is Easy' by Bjorn Lu blog post
- Learn HMR implementation and use cases
Where can I learn more about HMR?
